events.title: Car Photo in Black and White
must_haves: The entire image is neutral black and white, with no red remaining on the car or colour elsewhere.
The same compact hatchback remains in the same position and has unchanged body details.
The street and background objects retain their original positions and appearance apart from colour.
The full original composition is retained without cropping, in the photo's own shape.

answer_sheet.Black-and-white treatment: Neutral grayscale across the whole photo, not sepia or selective colour.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Everything except colour, including the car, street, background and full original framing.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One image in the original shape of the photo (5:3); free-tier resolution is fine.

events.text: The photo edit won't go through because my credits are used up, so I'll explain that. A local editor can desaturate the image instead, which is probably better anyway, since an AI edit would regenerate the picture and shrink it to 640px. I won't retry the AI edit.

I couldn't make the black-and-white version. Magic Hour turned down the edit because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and I have no link to give you.

To run it through Magic Hour, you'd need to add credits to your account. Then tell me and I'll run it again. Even then, the free plan would shrink the image to 640px wide and redraw it rather than just removing the colour, so small details could change slightly.

You can get an exact result for free by removing the colour on your own device:
- **Windows Photos:** Edit → Filter → choose a black-and-white filter.
- **Mac Preview:** Tools → Adjust Color → move the Saturation slider all the way left.
- **iPhone or Android Photos:** Edit → Filters → Mono or B&W, or set Saturation to its lowest setting.
- **Any web editor (e.g. Photopea):** Image → Adjustments → Desaturate.

Each of these only removes the colour and keeps your photo's original size, framing and detail.

events.why: The edit failed because the account lacks credits, so nothing was produced. The reply explains that limitation and suggests alternatives, rather than asking for a choice or for approval to proceed.
